key_insight: RXNGraphormer is confirmed to be reproducible and broadly transferable for reaction prediction, but its performance drops in heterogeneous or distribution-shifted external datasets. In short: it works well in familiar settings, yet robustness is limited when the data changes.
problem_solved: This paper addresses whether a published reaction-prediction model can be independently reproduced and whether it generalizes to external datasets beyond its original benchmark conditions.
method: Independent reproduction of RXNGraphormer results using the published setup and evaluation protocol.
Evaluation on external benchmark datasets to test transferability across reaction prediction tasks.
Comparison of model performance under standard versus heterogeneous/distribution-shifted data conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides evidence that RXNGraphormer is a reliable baseline in controlled environments. It also highlights the need to test models under real-world data shifts before deploying them in chemistry or other scientific domains.
visual_elements: A reproducibility check icon or pipeline showing 'published model -> independent replication -> verified results'
A side-by-side benchmark bar chart comparing original vs external dataset performance
A domain-shift diagram illustrating standard data versus heterogeneous/distribution-shifted data
A traffic-light style summary showing 'reproducible', 'transferable', and 'limited under shift'
paper_title: Reusability report: Assessment of reproducibility and applicability to external datasets for RXNGraphormer
paper_authors: Chonghuan Zhang, Majian Zeng, Qianghua Lin, Kuangbiao Liao
